The green numbers are our own reflection. Of 122 sessions, 88 are Direct (19 users) and 8 come from github.com (1 user - this repository and the owner's browser). The outside audience is 25 sessions / 14 users, up 2 sessions from 23/13: at this size that is noise, not growth, and the runner counts it green anyway.

The lost cycle is a machinery failure, not a site failure. 2026-11-20 is recorded 'site-down' with site=000, but the attempt log shows the host could not resolve opencode.ai, preflight could not fetch the price chart, and the 12:39 review run on the same machine completed while https://btc500.net/ returns 200 today. The runner retries the agent but not the health check, so one DNS blip cost a day of work and one more day without a valid verdict.

The ask loop is the automation's failure, not the owner's. 16 handovers and 4 sends in 26 days, and both link asks built on The Block's five-field contact form lapsed unsent (2026-11-17 and 2026-11-21). Every send was one paste and one button. A review that keeps issuing forms the owner does not fill is measuring the owner's patience, not the channel.

The 2026-11-19 X-poster ask was unexecutable as written: the plists run /bin/bash on a .mjs (launchd-pm.err.log: 'line 174: unexpected EOF') and their PATH omits /Users/philipkasapov/.local/bin, where browse lives ('browse status': "browse isn't on PATH"). Fixing node alone would have moved the failure from bash to spawn("browse") - the same silence as a dead email address.
questions: We shipped five page changes in seven days and gained 0 indexed pages and 0 non-brand clicks. What in the last three weeks of work was chosen because it could move a result, rather than because it could be finished?
18 of 22 pages are crawled and declined by Google, and Bing declines the homepage too. Why does the backlog still contain anything that is not a dated fact a stranger would search for?
If the only indexed URL is the homepage and it earns 6 brand clicks a week, what is the site for until 2026-11-29, and what exactly does a visitor get that they cannot get from a tweet?
Why has the reviewer handed over 16 asks in 26 days when the ledger shows only one-paste actions get sent, and what would it take to admit a channel is closed instead of restating it?

owner_asks.action: Open Terminal, paste the one line below, press return. It fixes both defects in the three scheduled X poster jobs (they run /bin/bash on a .mjs file, and their PATH has no ~/.local/bin where `browse` lives) and reloads them. One paste, one return, about 10 seconds. Then tell the cycle and it will read posts.json.
owner_asks.content: for s in am md pm; do l=net.btc500.x-post-$s; f=$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/$l.plist; launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/$l 2>/dev/null; /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Set :ProgramArguments:2 /usr/local/bin/node" -c "Set :EnvironmentVariables:PATH /usr/local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/Users/philipkasapov/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin" "$f"; launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) "$f"; done
